correctness.rationale: For all integers d>=2 and all -1<t<1, the radical formula gives positive semiaxes and exact identities c-u=t, v^2-u^2=dcu, c^2+v^2+cu/d=1. The transformed sphere constraint equals 1-dcu(s-1/d)^2 for every boundary direction; the only flat contact is -e_1 and curved contacts are latitude s=1/d with supporting normals radial in normalized coordinates. A d+1-point regular-simplex selection forms a centered isotropic John contact certificate. The weighted support inequalities, trace bound and AM-GM prove unique maximal volume among unrestricted ellipsoids, not only symmetric ones. Exact slicing proves the occupied fraction. Fixed-d thin-cap expansions and weak normal convergence at t=lambda/sqrt(d) prove the endpoint and Gaussian laws. Differentiating log G gives h-beta<0 from strictly positive variance of a truncated standard normal; Mills asymptotics prove its sharp terminal limit. The standalone checker passed 6922 diagnostic assertions; infinite claims rest on analytic proof.

value.rationale: The entire one-parameter natural family of spherical caps admits an explicit unrestricted optimizer and a finite universal isotropic contact frame, permitting exact geometric reconstruction of optimal occupied volumes. The nontrivial scaling is n^{-1/2} in the cap-height central-limit window, and its strictly decreasing, sharp Gaussian profile distinguishes the inscribed approximation from the known increasing enclosing-ellipsoid overhead. The sharp thin-cap dimension limit is a useful benchmark; neither arbitrary parameter slicing nor finite table recomputation is involved.
